questions.stem: A student picks up a book from the floor and places it on a high shelf. Which energy store has increased?
questions.explanation: Lifting the book increases its height above the ground, which increases its gravitational potential energy store. The kinetic energy store is zero once the book is at rest on the shelf. The chemical energy store in the student's muscles decreased to provide this energy, but the question asks which store increased.

questions.stem: A battery-powered toy car is moving along a flat surface. Which energy stores are decreasing and increasing respectively?

options.text: Chemical decreasing, kinetic and thermal increasing

questions.explanation: The battery's chemical energy store decreases as it powers the motor. The car's kinetic energy store increases as it moves, and the thermal energy store of the surroundings increases due to friction and resistance in the motor. Batteries store chemical energy, not nuclear energy.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of energy in the elastic potential energy store?

options.text: A ball rolling down a hill
A compressed spring in a toy launcher
A hot cup of tea cooling down

questions.explanation: A compressed spring stores elastic potential energy because it has been deformed from its natural shape. A ball rolling down a hill has kinetic and gravitational potential energy. A hot cup of tea has thermal energy. A torch converts chemical energy to light.

questions.stem: A firework rocket is launched upwards and explodes at its highest point. At the moment just before the explosion, which energy stores contain most of the energy originally in the chemical store of the fuel?

options.text: Gravitational potential, thermal, and chemical energy stores

questions.explanation: At the highest point, the rocket has gained gravitational potential energy from its height. Some chemical energy remains in the unexploded firework. Thermal energy has been transferred to the surroundings from the burning fuel. The kinetic energy is minimal at the highest point (momentarily at rest). Nuclear energy is not involved in chemical reactions.

questions.stem: Two identical balls are held at the same height. Ball A has a mass of 2 kg and Ball B has a mass of 4 kg. Which statement about their gravitational potential energy stores is correct?

options.text: Both balls have the same gravitational potential energy
Ball A has twice the gravitational potential energy of Ball B
Ball B has four times the gravitational potential energy of Ball A
Ball B has twice the gravitational potential energy of Ball A

questions.explanation: Gravitational potential energy = mass x gravitational field strength x height (GPE = mgh). Since both balls are at the same height and g is constant, GPE is directly proportional to mass. Ball B has double the mass, so it has double the GPE. It is not four times because GPE depends linearly on mass, not on mass squared.
